teaching.zh-Hans: 读“I am”和“:”前的名字。“I”指说话者。把描述与这个人对应，不要选话中提到的另一个名字。great表示很好，new to表示刚到某地，D.C.指华盛顿哥伦比亚特区。small town是小城镇，apartment是公寓住房，roommate是同住的人。
teaching.zh-Hant: 讀「I am」和「:」前的名字。「I」指說話者。把描述與這個人對應，不要選話中提到的另一個名字。great表示很好，new to表示剛到某地，D.C.指華盛頓哥倫比亞特區。small town是小城鎮，apartment是公寓住房，roommate是同住的人。
teaching.en: Read “I am” and the name before “:”. “I” means that speaker. Keep the description with that person, not another name in their words. Great means very well; new to a place means just arrived. D.C. is Washington, D.C. A small town is a small place to live. An apartment is a home in a building; a roommate shares a home.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 虚构示例：“Mira: I am happy. Leo: I am tired.” → 说自己开心的是Mira；说自己累了的是Leo。“I”指正在说话的人。happy表示开心，tired表示累。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 虛構示例：「Mira: I am happy. Leo: I am tired.」 → 說自己開心的是Mira；說自己累了的是Leo。「I」指正在說話的人。happy表示開心，tired表示累。
workedExample.en: Made-up example: “Mira: I am happy. Leo: I am tired.” → Says they are happy: Mira. Says they are tired: Leo. “I” means the person speaking. Happy means feeling good; tired means needing rest.

explanations.zh-Hans: 正确。“I am from a small town.”回答来自哪里。“new to D.C”表示刚到那里，不能据此判断来自那里。
explanations.zh-Hant: 正確。「I am from a small town.」回答來自哪裡。「new to D.C」表示剛到那裡，不能據此判斷來自那裡。
explanations.en: Yes. “I am from a small town.” answers “Where are you from?” “New to D.C” describes someone new there; it does not give their origin.

explanations.zh-Hans: “I come from D.C.”不是录音确认的描述。“I am from a small town.”回答来自哪里。“new to D.C”表示刚到那里，不能据此判断来自那里。
explanations.zh-Hant: 「I come from D.C.」不是錄音確認的描述。「I am from a small town.」回答來自哪裡。「new to D.C」表示剛到那裡，不能據此判斷來自那裡。
explanations.en: “I come from D.C.” is not the stated description. “I am from a small town.” answers “Where are you from?” “New to D.C” describes someone new there; it does not give their origin.

teaching.zh-Hans: 听完整回答。提到的词可能描述别的事情，也可能被否定。From表示来自，new to表示刚到某地，not表示否定。Book是书，pen是笔，big表示大。
teaching.zh-Hant: 聽完整回答。提到的詞可能描述別的事情，也可能被否定。From表示來自，new to表示剛到某地，not表示否定。Book是書，pen是筆，big表示大。
teaching.en: Listen to the whole answer. A mentioned word may describe something else or be ruled out. “From” tells where someone comes from. “New to” means new in a place. “Not” means no. A book is for reading; a pen is for writing. “Big” means large.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 虚构示例：“I am new to London. I am from York.”问来自哪里 → York。London是刚到的地方，不是所说的来源。“It is not a bag. It is a cup.”问是什么 → A cup。Bag被排除了。Cup是杯子，bag是袋子。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 虛構示例：「I am new to London. I am from York.」問來自哪裡 → York。London是剛到的地方，不是所說的來源。「It is not a bag. It is a cup.」問是什麼 → A cup。Bag被排除了。Cup是杯子，bag是袋子。
workedExample.en: Made-up example: “I am new to London. I am from York.” Where am I from? → York. London is where I am new, not my stated origin. “It is not a bag. It is a cup.” What is it? → A cup. A bag is ruled out. Cup means a thing that holds a drink; bag means a thing for carrying things.

goal.en: Read a small count and keep it with the right item.

teaching.zh-Hans: one=1，two=2，three=3，four=4。先看数的是什么。姓名用字母拼写；街道号码是地址，不是字母数量。return books是把书归还library（图书馆）；需要归还不等于已归还。errand是在外办的小事。
teaching.zh-Hant: one=1，two=2，three=3，four=4。先看數的是什麼。姓名用字母拼寫；街道號碼是地址，不是字母數量。return books是把書歸還library（圖書館）；需要歸還不等於已歸還。errand是在外辦的小事。
teaching.en: One=1, two=2, three=3, four=4. Read what is counted. A name is spelled with letters; a street number is an address, not a letter count. Return books means take them back to the library. Need to return does not mean already returned. An errand is a small task outside home.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 虚构示例：“I need to return four keys.” → 需要归还多少把钥匙？4把。four对应keys（钥匙），没有说已经归还。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 虛構示例：「I need to return four keys.」 → 需要歸還多少把鑰匙？4把。four對應keys（鑰匙），沒有說已經歸還。
workedExample.en: Made-up example: “I need to return four keys.” → How many keys? 4. Keep four with keys. This does not say the keys have been returned.

goal.zh-Hans: 找到题目所问事情的书面时刻。
goal.zh-Hant: 找到題目所問事情的書面時刻。
goal.en: Find the written clock time for the asked event.

teaching.zh-Hans: 对照问题和时刻陈述。7:35中，7是小时，35是分钟；a.m.从午夜至中午之前，p.m.从中午至午夜之前；midnight是午夜，noon是中午12:00。保留原文明说的时段，未说时不要补写。busy表示忙，writing表示写；lunch是午餐，boss是上司。maybe later表示也许稍后，不是确定的时间。
teaching.zh-Hant: 對照問題和時刻陳述。7:35中，7是小時，35是分鐘；a.m.從午夜至中午之前，p.m.從中午至午夜之前；midnight是午夜，noon是中午12:00。保留原文明說的時段，未說時不要補寫。busy表示忙，writing表示寫；lunch是午餐，boss是上司。maybe later表示也許稍後，不是確定的時間。
teaching.en: Read the question and its time statement. In 7:35, 7 is the hour and 35 the minutes. A.m. runs from midnight to before noon; p.m. runs from noon to before midnight. Midnight is 12 at night; noon is 12:00 midday. Keep an explicit period; do not add one when absent. Busy means working; writing means putting words down. Lunch is a midday meal; a boss leads work. Maybe later is not a confirmed time.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 虚构示例：“Our lesson is at 8:20 p.m.” → 上课时刻是8:20p.m.，保留晚间标记。“What time is it now? 8:05.” → 现在是8:05，不能换成上课时刻或补写时段。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 虛構示例：「Our lesson is at 8:20 p.m.」 → 上課時刻是8:20p.m.，保留晚間標記。「What time is it now? 8:05.」 → 現在是8:05，不能換成上課時刻或補寫時段。
workedExample.en: Made-up example: “Our lesson is at 8:20 p.m.” → Lesson time: 8:20 p.m., with the stated evening period. “What time is it now? 8:05.” → Current time: 8:05; do not replace it with lesson time or add a period.

nextStep.en: Read the other original without hints. Keep its event, clock digits and any stated period.

Anna: Oh, Pete. This is not the gym.
Pete: That’s right, Anna. This is the mailroom.

Anna: Hi! Today, my friend Ashley, is coming over. I am showing her my new apartment! Oh! That’s Ashley calling.
Anna: Hi Ashley!
Ashley: Hi Anna! I’m coming to your apartment. Where is your apartment?
Anna: My apartment is near the Columbia Heights Metro.
Ashley: It is near the Columbia Heights Metro?
Anna: Yes. Exit the Metro and turn right. Then at the bus station turn left. Then walk straight ahead.

questions.prompt:

Exit the Metro. What next?
options: Turn left.
Turn right.

explanations.zh-Hans: 这改变了地点关系或动作。出Metro后右转；到bus station后才左转。不能交换步骤与地点。
explanations.zh-Hant: 這改變了地點關係或動作。出Metro後右轉；到bus station後才左轉。不能交換步驟與地點。
explanations.en: This changes a relation or action. After exiting the Metro, turn right. Turn left later, at the bus station. Keep the steps and places together.

teaching.zh-Hans: 读完整指令。exit表示离开；turn right是右转，turn left是左转；walk straight ahead是向前直走。保留每次转弯对应的地点。boss是上司，co-workers是同事，meet them在这里是认识他们，不是替他们工作。busy表示正忙。指令不代表动作已经完成。
teaching.zh-Hant: 讀完整指令。exit表示離開；turn right是右轉，turn left是左轉；walk straight ahead是向前直走。保留每次轉彎對應的地點。boss是上司，co-workers是同事，meet them在這裡是認識他們，不是替他們工作。busy表示正忙。指令不代表動作已經完成。
teaching.en: Read the whole instruction. Exit means leave. Turn right or left, then walk straight ahead: go forward. Keep the place for each turn. A boss gives work instructions; co-workers work with you. Meet them means get to know them, not do their work. Busy means working now. A request does not mean it happened.

workedExample.zh-Hant: 虛構示例：「Leave the shop. Turn left at the gate. Then turn right at the park.」 → 大門處左轉，公園處右轉。「Please greet your neighbour.」要求向鄰居問好，沒有說已經問好。
workedExample.en: Made-up example: “Leave the shop. Turn left at the gate. Then turn right at the park.” → At the gate: left. At the park: right. “Please greet your neighbour.” → Say hello to the neighbour; this does not say the greeting happened.

teaching.zh-Hans: 听完问句及回答，问句不等于确认。No之后逐个核对纠正的字母或数字。Two N’s表示字母N有两个；电话号码是一串数字，不是数量。数字词：zero=0、one=1、two=2、three=3、four=4、five=5、six=6、seven=7、eight=8、nine=9。字母N的名称读作“en”。
teaching.zh-Hant: 聽完問句及回答，問句不等於確認。No之後逐個核對糾正的字母或數字。Two N’s表示字母N有兩個；電話號碼是一串數字，不是數量。數字詞：zero=0、one=1、two=2、three=3、four=4、five=5、six=6、seven=7、eight=8、nine=9。字母N的名稱讀作「en」。
teaching.en: Listen to the question and the answer. A question is not a confirmed fact. After “No”, check every letter or digit in the correction. “Two N’s” means the letter N occurs twice. A phone number is a sequence of digits, not a count. Number words: zero=0, one=1, two=2, three=3, four=4, five=5, six=6, seven=7, eight=8, nine=9. The letter N is said “en”.

workedExample.zh-Hant: 示例：「Is it 777-1111? No, it is 777-1122.」問確認哪個號碼 → 777-1122。第一個只是被詢問後否定的號碼。核對末兩位，其他數字不變。
workedExample.en: Example: “Is it 777-1111? No, it is 777-1122.” Which number is confirmed? → 777-1122. The first number was asked about and rejected. Compare the last two digits; keep the rest unchanged.

blocks.text:
Marsha: Hey, Anna, my friend is having a party on Saturday. Can you come with me?

Anna: Sorry, I can’t come with you. I have to get my driver’s license.

Marsha: Will you be busy all day?

Anna: I don’t know. First, I have to take a test on the computer. Then I have to take a test in the car.

Marsha: But you have to take the test during the day, don't you?

Anna: Yes.

Marsha: The party is at night.

Anna: Oh. Then I can come with you to the party on Saturday night.

Marsha: Great! I have to help my friend with the party. Can you help me?

Anna: Sure. That sounds like fun.

blocks.text:
Anna: Hello! DC is a city for walking. In our neighborhood, I can do all my errands. Marsha, before we get ice cream, I need to return three books to the library. Where is the library?
Marsha: It is on this street on the corner.
Anna: Awesome!
Marsha: Let's go!
Anna: Marsha, I can return the books here.
Marsha: Anna, what are those in the books?

questions.prompt: What is the planned order of these actions?
options: get ice cream → return three books to the library

explanations.zh-Hans: 这改变了地点关系或动作。“before we get ice cream, I need to return three books”表示先还书，再买冰淇淋。before从句虽然先写出，其中的动作在计划中却较晚。需要还书不证明已经还书；另一选项颠倒先后。
explanations.zh-Hant: 這改變了地點關係或動作。「before we get ice cream, I need to return three books」表示先還書，再買冰淇淋。before從句雖然先寫出，其中的動作在計劃中卻較晚。需要還書不證明已經還書；另一選項顛倒先後。
explanations.en: This changes a relation or action. “Before we get ice cream, I need to return three books” puts returning the books first. The before-clause occurs earlier on the page but its action comes later in the plan. Needing to return books does not prove they were returned. The other option reverses that order.

blocks.text: Philip had to walk some five miles before he reached a little station, where he could wait for a train, and he had ample time for reflection.

questions.prompt: Listen. Which action order is stated?
options: reach a little station → walk some five miles
walk some five miles → reach a little station

explanations.zh-Hans: 动作先后颠倒了。Philip先步行约五英里，才到达车站。reached确认到达；仅有had to只表示需要。some five是大约五，不是精确测量。could wait表示可以等车，不证明已经等车。把步行与到站反序会改变before。
explanations.zh-Hant: 動作先後顛倒了。Philip先步行約五英里，才到達車站。reached確認到達；僅有had to只表示需要。some five是大約五，不是精確測量。could wait表示可以等車，不證明已經等車。把步行與到站反序會改變before。
explanations.en: The actions are reversed. Philip’s walk of some five miles comes before reaching the station. “Reached” establishes arrival; had to alone would only state a requirement. teaching.zh-Hans: before表示一事早于另一事，要按时间而非只按文字排列。核对后一个动作确实发生；意图、需要或可能本身不能证明完成。这是虚构人物的行程。passed the door是经过门口；a dozen是十二；courage是勇气；made a dash是快速行动；did it回指上前敲门。master在这里是受侍奉的主人；my dear是称呼。some five miles是约五英里；station是车站；ample time for reflection是有充分时间思考。
teaching.zh-Hant: before表示一事早於另一事，要按時間而非只按文字排列。核對後一個動作確實發生；意圖、需要或可能本身不能證明完成。這是虛構人物的行程。passed the door是經過門口；a dozen是十二；courage是勇氣；made a dash是快速行動；did it回指上前敲門。master在這裡是受侍奉的主人；my dear是稱呼。some five miles是約五英里；station是車站；ample time for reflection是有充分時間思考。
teaching.en: Before puts one event earlier than another. Follow time, not just word order. Confirm the later action in the source: an intention, requirement or possibility alone is not completion. These are fictional journeys. Passed the door means went past it; a dozen means twelve; courage means being brave; made a dash means moved quickly; did it refers back to the approach and knock. Master means the person served in this household; my dear is a form of address. Some five miles means about five miles; a station is where trains stop; ample time for reflection means enough time to think.

blocks.text:
Marsha: Hey, Anna, my friend is having a party on Saturday. Can you come with me?

Anna: Sorry, I can’t come with you. I have to get my driver’s license.

Marsha: Will you be busy all day?

Anna: I don’t know. First, I have to take a test on the computer. Then I have to take a test in the car.

Marsha: But you have to take the test during the day, don't you?

Anna: Yes.

Marsha: The party is at night.

Anna: Oh. Then I can come with you to the party on Saturday night.

Marsha: Great! I have to help my friend with the party. Can you help me?

Anna: Sure. That sounds like fun.

Anna: Oh! Excuse me. I am Anna Matteo from The News. Do you have time for a couple of questions?

Louis: Sure!

Anna: Are you from Washington, D.C.?

Louis: No, I’m not.

Anna: What is your name and where are you from?

Louis: My name is Louis. And I’m from China.

Anna: What languages do you speak?

Louis: I speak Chinese and English.

Anna: What do you like about Washington DC?

Louis: I like the museums. I really like the art museums.

Anna: Many of the museums are free.

Louis: I like that too!

Anna: Awesome! Thanks for your time, Louis.

Louis: You’re very welcome. Bye!

need.zh-Hans: need to和have to表示需要或必须做。保留说话者及before（在……之前）条件；一个人的需要不能换给另一个人。需要做不表示已经做，也不一定表示想做。driver’s license是驾照；errands是在外办的小事；return books是把书归还library（图书馆）。invitation是邀请，同意参加不等于其他需要被取消。
need.zh-Hant: need to和have to表示需要或必須做。保留說話者及before（在……之前）條件；一個人的需要不能換給另一個人。需要做不表示已經做，也不一定表示想做。driver’s license是駕照；errands是在外辦的小事；return books是把書歸還library（圖書館）。invitation是邀請，同意參加不等於其他需要被取消。
need.en: Need to and have to state a requirement. Keep the speaker and any before-clause: one person’s requirement is not another person’s. A requirement is not proof of completion or of wanting to do it. Driver’s license means permission to drive; errands are small tasks outside home; return books means take them back to the library. An invitation asks someone to join; accepting it does not cancel other requirements.

preference.zh-Hans: like表示喜欢，really like表示很喜欢。保留人物及具体地方。“都很好”是总体评价，不是特别说喜欢哪一个。“I like X”不等于“只喜欢X”“最喜欢X”或“讨厌Y”。museum是博物馆；art museum展示艺术品；sculpture是立体雕塑；Sculpture Garden是户外雕塑花园。free admission表示免门票。
preference.zh-Hant: like表示喜歡，really like表示很喜歡。保留人物及具體地方。「都很好」是總體評價，不是特別說喜歡哪一個。「I like X」不等於「只喜歡X」「最喜歡X」或「討厭Y」。museum是博物館；art museum展示藝術品；sculpture是立體雕塑；Sculpture Garden是戶外雕塑花園。free admission表示免門票。
preference.en: Like states a preference; really like strengthens it. Keep the person and the named place. “All are good” is a general evaluation, not a particular preference. “I like X” does not mean “only X”, “X is my favourite”, or “I dislike Y”. Museums display objects; art museums display art; sculptures are three-dimensional artworks. The Sculpture Garden is an outdoor place for sculptures; free admission means no entry charge.

need.zh-Hans: 不计分虚构示例：“Lina needs to buy milk before making breakfast. Omar has to clean the table.” → Lina需要在做早饭之前买牛奶；擦桌子是Omar需要做的事。这里没有说已买牛奶，也没有说Lina喜欢购物。
need.zh-Hant: 不計分虛構示例：「Lina needs to buy milk before making breakfast. Omar has to clean the table.」 → Lina需要在做早飯之前買牛奶；擦桌子是Omar需要做的事。這裡沒有說已買牛奶，也沒有說Lina喜歡購物。
need.en: Unscored made-up example: “Lina needs to buy milk before making breakfast. Omar has to clean the table.” Lina’s required action is buying milk, before breakfast. Cleaning the table belongs to Omar. This does not say milk was bought, or that Lina likes shopping.

preference.zh-Hans: 不计分虚构示例：“Both cafés are good. Noor says: I like the Riverside Café.” → Noor明说喜欢Riverside咖啡馆。“两家都好”没有特别说喜欢另一家，也没有说明只喜欢这家、最喜欢这家，或讨厌另一家。
preference.zh-Hant: 不計分虛構示例：「Both cafés are good. Noor says: I like the Riverside Café.」 → Noor明說喜歡Riverside咖啡館。「兩家都好」沒有特別說喜歡另一家，也沒有說明只喜歡這家、最喜歡這家，或討厭另一家。
preference.en: Unscored made-up example: “Both cafés are good. Noor says: I like the Riverside Café.” Noor explicitly likes Riverside. “Both are good” does not explicitly name a liking for the other café. Nothing says Riverside is Noor’s only or favourite café, or that Noor dislikes the other one.

preference.zh-Hans: like/liked表示喜欢，liked指过去。保留人物、对象及代词指向，不补写只喜欢、最喜欢或讨厌。music是音乐；violinist是小提琴演奏者；bore指乏味的人，impatiently指不耐烦地。lonesome是远离人群的，crowded是拥挤的；suitable是适合的，meditation是静思，accustomed是习惯于，anxious是担心的。这些陈述来自虚构人物。
preference.zh-Hant: like/liked表示喜歡，liked指過去。保留人物、對象及代詞指向，不補寫只喜歡、最喜歡或討厭。music是音樂；violinist是小提琴演奏者；bore指乏味的人，impatiently指不耐煩地。lonesome是遠離人群的，crowded是擁擠的；suitable是適合的，meditation是靜思，accustomed是習慣於，anxious是擔心的。這些陳述來自虛構人物。
preference.en: Like/liked states liking; liked refers to the past. Keep the person, object and pronoun reference. Do not add only, favourite or dislike. Music is sound made for listening; a violinist plays a violin. Bore means an uninteresting person; impatiently means without patience. Lonesome means away from other people; crowded means full of people. Suitable means good for a purpose; meditation is quiet thought; accustomed means used to something; anxious means worried. These statements belong to fictional characters.

Caty: Okay, Jonathan, you will buy the first dish. Here is $10. Surprise us!

Jonathan: Okay, I’ll be back in 15 minutes.

Anna: What country do I want to visit?

Caty: Anna, you pick the second country. Here is $10.

Anna: I want chicken.

Caty: The food truck, over there, has great chicken.

Anna: Awesome!

Caty: After you buy your food, meet me here.

Jonathan: Excuse me, I’ll have the shrimp.

Jonathan: Oh, you’re out of shrimp. Okay, I’ll have the beef then.

Anna: Hello. I want the chicken dish.

Truck worker: We're out of chicken.

Anna: You're out of chicken.

Worker: Yep.

Anna: I’ll try another food truck. Thanks!

Worker: You're welcome.

credit.attribution: Lesson 21: Can You Come to the Party? — VOA Learning English. VOA Learning English (https://learningenglish.voanews.com/a/lets-learn-english-lesson-21-can-you-come-to-the-party/3406732.html).

blocks.text:
Marsha: Hey, Anna, my friend is having a party on Saturday. Can you come with me?

Anna: Sorry, I can’t come with you. I have to get my driver’s license.

Marsha: Will you be busy all day?

Anna: I don’t know. First, I have to take a test on the computer. Then I have to take a test in the car.

Marsha: But you have to take the test during the day, don't you?

Anna: Yes.

Marsha: The party is at night.

Anna: Oh. Then I can come with you to the party on Saturday night.

Marsha: Great! I have to help my friend with the party. Can you help me?

Anna: Sure. That sounds like fun.

teaching.en: Follow the same person from the first statement to the later one. New information can change a reply or request without changing an external event. Can/cannot state possibility; I’ll have names a food order, not food already received. Driver’s license is permission to drive; the computer/car tests are the planned tasks; during the day contrasts with at night. Here Caty sends colleagues to buy dishes: a dish is a portion of food, shrimp is seafood, beef is cow meat, chicken is poultry, out of means unavailable, and a food truck sells meals from a vehicle.
teaching.zh-Hans: 先找到同一人物的原先陈述，再读补充信息及后来的陈述。新信息可以改变回复或要求，不一定表示外部事件改变。can/cannot表示能否；I’ll have在这里是点餐，不是已经吃到。driver’s license是驾照；computer/car tests是计划的电脑／路考；during the day与at night区分白天／晚上。Caty让同事买菜品；dish是一份食物，shrimp是虾，beef是牛肉，chicken是鸡肉，out of表示售完，food truck是售餐车。
teaching.zh-Hant: 先找到同一人物的原先陳述，再讀補充資訊及後來的陳述。新資訊可以改變回覆或要求，不一定表示外部事件改變。can/cannot表示能否；I’ll have在這裡是點餐，不是已經吃到。driver’s license是駕照；computer/car tests是計劃的電腦／路考；during the day與at night區分白天／晚上。Caty讓同事買菜品；dish是一份食物，shrimp是蝦，beef是牛肉，chicken是雞肉，out of表示售完，food truck是售餐車。

teaching.zh-Hans: 追踪同一事物的变化。no longer表示原先状态不再持续；have been removed表示东西已被移走。保留原先→更新的方向，不补写录音没说的修复或返回。灯泡段落讨论白炽灯；filament是内部细灯丝，operation是运作，burns out是烧坏而停止工作，eventually是最终，hundreds没有给出确切小时数。博物馆说明中fabulous riches指大量财富或贵重物品，tomb是墓，it回指墓；Cairo是开罗。识别录音所报告的情况，不补写搬移日期或当作实时参观信息。
teaching.zh-Hant: 追蹤同一事物的變化。no longer表示原先狀態不再持續；have been removed表示東西已被移走。保留原先→更新的方向，不補寫錄音沒說的修復或返回。燈泡段落討論白熾燈；filament是內部細燈絲，operation是運作，burns out是燒壞而停止工作，eventually是最終，hundreds沒有給出確切小時數。博物館說明中fabulous riches指大量財富或貴重物品，tomb是墓，it回指墓；Cairo是開羅。識別錄音所報告的情況，不補寫搬移日期或當作即時參觀資訊。

The bulb context is the incandescent type: filament means the thin wire inside; operation means working; burns out means stops working; eventually means in the end. Hundreds gives no exact number of hours. In the museum description, fabulous riches means great wealth or valuable objects; a tomb is a burial place; it points back to the tomb. Cairo is the named city. Identify what this recording reports, without adding a movement date or treating it as live visitor information.

teaching.en: Because introduces a reason for an action or statement. First find the asked person and action; then keep the stated reason, rather than treating a habit or nearby background as its cause. Today’s activity can differ from a usual habit; will try states a plan, not completion. A drum band plays percussion; a puppet show uses small figures to perform a story. Shakespeare is a writer’s name; a birthday is the day someone was born. Jog means run slowly; try means attempt. Always, sometimes and never describe frequency; a later correction replaces an earlier one.

teaching.zh-Hant: because後接從句，because of後接名詞短語，都可給出原因。先認準題目所問人物／動作或詞，旁邊細節或另一層理由不能互換。這是動物書：Peter Rabbit在想Grandfather Frog剛才的話，另一段描寫一隻鼠。gossip指愛議論別人的人，wondered是心裡疑問；cheek是臉頰，pocket是小囊，lined with hair指裡面襯著毛；coat在這裡是毛皮，fineness是細密，softness是柔軟。名稱中所問部分與另一部分也要區分。
teaching.en: Because plus a clause and because of plus a noun phrase give reasons. First identify the asked person/action or word; a nearby detail or another reason is not interchangeable. These are animal books: Peter Rabbit is thinking about Grandfather Frog’s remark; the other description names a mouse. A gossip talks about other people; wondered means thought about a question. A cheek is a side of the face; a pocket is a small pouch; lined with hair means hair inside. A coat here means fur; fineness means delicate texture and softness means not rough or hard. Keep the asked part of a name separate from another part.

blocks.text:
Caty: This is the News. Happy and sad are feelings. You can’t have them in The News.

Anna: Okay. I got it.

Caty: Okay. Let’s try the third story. She’s reading the third story!

Anna: Hello and welcome to The News.

City politicians in Big Town are using city money to have a big party on a cruise ship. They are taking the money for the party from the children’s library.

Anna: What?! That makes me very angry.

Caty: No, no, no! Anna, you cannot say you are angry! This is The News!!!

blocks.text:
Marsha: Great! I have to help my friend with the party. Can you help me?

Anna: Sure. That sounds like fun.

Marsha: Everyone has to bring something or do something. You can bring food, or you can perform.

questions.prompt:
Read the stated rule.
Which summary keeps the stated rule and its scope?
options: At this party, everyone must both bring food and perform.
At this party, everyone must contribute; bringing food or performing is an option.

explanations.zh-Hans: 这改变了地点关系或动作。每个人都要为这次聚会出一份力。or连接选择：带食物或表演是给出的选项，不是要求每人同时完成两项。这里也没有禁止两项都做，没有证明Anna已经贡献。
explanations.zh-Hant: 這改變了地點關係或動作。每個人都要為這次聚會出一份力。or連接選擇：帶食物或表演是給出的選項，不是要求每人同時完成兩項。這裡也沒有禁止兩項都做，沒有證明Anna已經貢獻。
explanations.en: This changes a relation or action. Everyone has to contribute to this party. Or gives alternatives: bringing food and performing are named options, not two duties that everyone must do together. The rule does not ban doing both, and does not prove Anna has already contributed.

teaching.zh-Hans: 先找谁提出规则、谁遵守、需要或禁止什么，以及适用场合。have to表示要求；cannot可表示限制。or给出选择，本身没有禁止两项都做。不能把特定场合的规则扩大为任何地方都禁止，也不能把不准说某种感受改成不准有这种感受。contribute是出一份力，perform是表演；facts是事实信息，feelings是情绪。The News是对话中的节目，Big Town故事是虚构新闻片段，不是已核实的报道。
teaching.zh-Hant: 先找誰提出規則、誰遵守、需要或禁止什麼，以及適用場合。have to表示要求；cannot可表示限制。or給出選擇，本身沒有禁止兩項都做。不能把特定場合的規則擴大為任何地方都禁止，也不能把不准說某種感受改成不准有這種感受。contribute是出一份力，perform是表演；facts是事實資訊，feelings是情緒。The News是對話中的節目，Big Town故事是虛構新聞片段，不是已核實的報道。
teaching.en: Find who sets the rule, who follows it, the required or restricted action, and where it applies. Have to marks a requirement; cannot can express a restriction. Or offers alternatives and does not by itself ban doing both. Do not turn a setting-specific rule into a ban everywhere, or a restriction on saying something into a ban on feeling it. Contribute means give something or help; perform means present music, acting or another act. Facts are information; feelings are emotions. The News is the programme in this dialogue. Its Big Town story is a fictional news item, not a verified report.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 不计分虚构示例：“In this reading room, visitors must silence their phones. They may read a book or a magazine.” 要求是在这个阅览室把手机静音；书或杂志是选择，没有要求两种都读，也没有禁止都读。没有说明咖啡馆的手机规则，或访客已遵守。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 不計分虛構示例：「In this reading room, visitors must silence their phones. They may read a book or a magazine.」要求是在這個閱覽室把手機靜音；書或雜誌是選擇，沒有要求兩種都讀，也沒有禁止都讀。沒有說明咖啡館的手機規則，或訪客已遵守。
workedExample.en: Unscored made-up example: “In this reading room, visitors must silence their phones. They may read a book or a magazine.” Required: silence phones in this room. Options: book or magazine; the rule does not require both or ban reading both. It says nothing about phones in the café or whether a visitor has complied.

teaching.zh-Hans: requires表示必须做；could choose／may及or表示选择。把before／after与动作对应，保留执行者：模拟系统不会改变某项，不等于禁止玩家改变。录音描述游戏。building lot是建筑地块，designate是划定或指定，resident是居民，class是游戏类别，simulation是电脑模拟；stage是游戏关卡，continue是继续，switch是更换；Dr. Mario、Dr. Peach和Dr. Bowser是角色名。理解录音中的描述，不推定当前可玩，也不补写所述条件之前的限制。
teaching.zh-Hant: requires表示必須做；could choose／may及or表示選擇。把before／after與動作對應，保留執行者：模擬系統不會改變某項，不等於禁止玩家改變。錄音描述遊戲。building lot是建築地塊，designate是劃定或指定，resident是居民，class是遊戲類別，simulation是電腦模擬；stage是遊戲關卡，continue是繼續，switch是更換；Dr. Mario、Dr. Peach和Dr. Bowser是角色名。理解錄音中的描述，不推定目前可玩，也不補寫所述條件之前的限制。
teaching.en: Requires marks a necessary action; could choose/may and or describe options. Keep before/after with the action, and keep the actor: a simulation not changing something is different from a player being forbidden to change it. These recordings describe games. A building lot is an area for a building; designate means mark or assign it. A resident lives there; class is a game category; simulation is the computer model. A stage is a game level; continue means keep using; switch means change. Dr. Mario, Dr. Peach and Dr. Bowser are character names. Interpret the recorded description without assuming current availability or adding restrictions before the stated condition.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 不计分虚构示例：“Before entering the pool, visitors must shower. Afterwards they may swim or sit by the pool.” 先淋浴是要求；之后游泳是选择，不是必须。没有要求游泳和坐着两项都做，也没有证明访客已经淋浴。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 不計分虛構示例：「Before entering the pool, visitors must shower. Afterwards they may swim or sit by the pool.」先淋浴是要求；之後游泳是選擇，不是必須。沒有要求游泳和坐著兩項都做，也沒有證明訪客已經淋浴。
workedExample.en: Unscored made-up example: “Before entering the pool, visitors must shower. Afterwards they may swim or sit by the pool.” Showering is required first; swimming is optional, not compulsory. The rule says nothing about requiring both swimming and sitting, or whether a visitor has already showered.

blocks.text:
Marsha: Will you be busy all day?

Anna: I don’t know. First, I have to take a test on the computer. Then I have to take a test in the car.

Marsha: But you have to take the test during the day, don't you?

Anna: Yes.

Marsha: The party is at night.

Anna: Oh. Then I can come with you to the party on Saturday night.

Marsha: Great! I have to help my friend with the party. Can you help me?

Anna: Sure. That sounds like fun.

Marsha: Everyone has to bring something or do something. You can bring food, or you can perform.

questions.prompt:
Combine two stated clues.
Which summary combines the party timing and contribution rule?
options: The party is on Saturday night; everyone must contribute, with food or a performance as options.
The party is on Saturday night; everyone must both bring food and perform.
The party is during the day on Saturday; everyone must contribute, with food or a performance as options.
The party is during the day on Saturday; everyone must both bring food and perform.

teaching.zh-Hans: 先看题目要求组合哪两条信息，再为每条各找一处原文线索；摘要必须两条都吻合，不能用一半正确抵消另一半错误。图书馆材料要保留before的先后关系及位置：this street是说话者所在的这条街，on the corner是在街道交会的拐角；errands是办些小事，return books是把借的书还回去。聚会材料要同时保留时间和贡献规则；or给出选择，没有要求两项都做，也没有禁止都做。计划及规则不证明动作已经完成。
teaching.zh-Hant: 先看題目要求組合哪兩條資訊，再為每條各找一處原文線索；摘要必須兩條都吻合，不能用一半正確抵消另一半錯誤。圖書館材料要保留before的先後關係及位置：this street是說話者所在的這條街，on the corner是在街道交會的拐角；errands是辦些小事，return books是把借的書還回去。聚會材料要同時保留時間和貢獻規則；or給出選擇，沒有要求兩項都做，也沒有禁止都做。計劃及規則不證明動作已經完成。
teaching.en: Read the question for the two details it asks you to combine. Find one source clue for each; a summary must match both. One correct half cannot repair a wrong other half. For the library, keep the before relation and the stated location; this street means the street the speakers are on, and on the corner means where streets meet. Errands are small tasks; return books means take borrowed books back. For the party, keep the stated time and contribution rule. Or gives alternatives without requiring or forbidding both. These statements describe plans and rules, not proof of completed actions.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 不计分虚构示例：“The art club meets on Tuesday. Bring a pencil.” 两条都保留是“星期二＋铅笔”；“星期二＋画笔”只保留日期，“星期五＋铅笔”只保留物品，“星期五＋画笔”两条都错。通知没有证明谁已参加或已带物品。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 不計分虛構示例：「The art club meets on Tuesday. Bring a pencil.」兩條都保留是「星期二＋鉛筆」；「星期二＋畫筆」只保留日期，「星期五＋鉛筆」只保留物品，「星期五＋畫筆」兩條都錯。通知沒有證明誰已參加或已帶物品。
workedExample.en: Unscored made-up example: “The art club meets on Tuesday. Bring a pencil.” Combine both: Tuesday + pencil. Tuesday + paintbrush matches only the day; Friday + pencil matches only the item; Friday + paintbrush matches neither. The notice does not prove anyone attended or brought an item.

teaching.zh-Hans: 先认准题目问哪两条信息，再为每条各听一处线索；每个选项的两个部分都要核对，不能用一半正确抵消另一半错误。apartment是楼里的住宅，D7是所说房号，不是完整地址，也没有证明说话者实际站在哪里；have to go表示需要离开，不表示已经走了。另一录音的riches指贵重物品，tomb是墓，it回指墓；no longer表示原先状态已结束，have been removed表示已被移走，Cairo是开罗。保留录音报告的两条信息，不据此核实时下馆藏。
teaching.zh-Hant: 先認準題目問哪兩條資訊，再為每條各聽一處線索；每個選項的兩個部分都要核對，不能用一半正確抵消另一半錯誤。apartment是樓裡的住宅，D7是所說房號，不是完整地址，也沒有證明說話者實際站在哪裡；have to go表示需要離開，不表示已經走了。另一錄音的riches指貴重物品，tomb是墓，it回指墓；no longer表示原先狀態已結束，have been removed表示已被移走，Cairo是開羅。保留錄音報告的兩條資訊，不據此核實時下館藏。
teaching.en: Identify the two details asked for; listen for one clue for each. Check both halves of every option. One correct half cannot repair a wrong other half. Apartment means a home within a building; D7 is the named unit, not a full address or proof of the speaker’s physical position. Have to go states a need, not completed departure. In the other recording, riches means valuable objects, tomb is a burial place, and it points back to the tomb. No longer means the former state has ended; have been removed reports movement away; Cairo is the named city. Keep what this recording reports without claiming a current museum location.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 不计分虚构示例：“The coach is blue. It leaves at ten.” 两条都吻合是“蓝色＋十点”；“蓝色＋十一点”只保留颜色，“红色＋十点”只保留时间，“红色＋十一点”两条都错。陈述没有证明大巴已出发。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 不計分虛構示例：「The coach is blue. It leaves at ten.」兩條都吻合是「藍色＋十點」；「藍色＋十一點」只保留顏色，「紅色＋十點」只保留時間，「紅色＋十一點」兩條都錯。陳述沒有證明大巴已出發。
workedExample.en: Unscored made-up example: “The coach is blue. It leaves at ten.” Both clues: blue + ten. Blue + eleven keeps only the colour; red + ten keeps only the time; red + eleven changes both. The statement does not prove the coach has already left.

blocks.text: Goals can be big or small. A goal can range from I am going to write one extra page tonight, to I am going to work to get an A in this course, all the way to I am going to graduate in the top of my class so I can start my career with a really good position. The great thing about goals is that they can include and influence a number of other things that all work toward a much bigger picture. For example, if your goal is to get an A in a certain course, all the reading, studying, and every assignment you do for that course contributes to the larger goal. You have motivation to do each of those things and to do them well.

blocks.text: To begin to read, write, and think critically, it is helpful to look at something familiar such as social media and the way it is used. Interactions on social media, as in all types of conversation, present rhetorical situations that form the basis of communication. In the most basic terms, a rhetorical situation has two elements: agents and conditions. Agents are the originators (initiators) and the audience of the communication. The originator may have a real audience or an anticipated audience. A real audience is made up of people the originator may know personally or know of. For example, if you are the originator, your real audience could be a group of your peers to whom you present your ideas in class. Or it could be a person to whom you send a text message. You know the members of the class and know something about them. Similarly, you know the person to whom you send the text. An anticipated audience is one you hope to reach or one you expect will engage with your communication. When you post on social media platforms, for instance, your audience is probably anticipated. While you might have followers, you may not know them personally, but you anticipate who they are and how they might react.

teaching.zh-Hans: 主旨概括这段连贯材料在说明什么；细节或例子只支持其中一部分。用相关例子核对概括句，保留否定、can／may以及generally／probably等限制。细节即使真实，也可能不能回答主旨题。goal是目标，assignment是课程任务；originator是沟通发起者，audience是受众，anticipated是预期的，peers是同类群体中的人。录音中appeal是提出请求的动词，summon是叫人过来；aid是援助，victims是受不利事件影响的人，government是政府。supervisor是工作主管，principal是校长；a moment是短暂一会儿，不是固定秒数。
teaching.zh-Hant: 主旨概括這段連貫材料在說明什麼；細節或例子只支持其中一部分。用相關例子核對概括句，保留否定、can／may以及generally／probably等限制。細節即使真實，也可能不能回答主旨題。goal是目標，assignment是課程任務；originator是溝通發起者，audience是受眾，anticipated是預期的，peers是同類群體中的人。錄音中appeal是提出請求的動詞，summon是叫人過來；aid是援助，victims是受不利事件影響的人，government是政府。supervisor是工作主管，principal是校長；a moment是短暫一會兒，不是固定秒數。
teaching.en: A main point covers what the connected excerpt explains; a detail or example supports only part of it. Check a broad statement against all the relevant examples and keep negation, can/may and words such as generally or probably. A detail can be true and still fail a main-point question. Goal means an aim; an assignment is a course task. An originator starts communication; an audience receives it; anticipated means expected and peers are people in a similar group. In the recordings, appeal is a verb for making a request, while summon means call someone to come. Aid is help, victims are people affected by a harmful event, and government means the public authority. A supervisor is a person overseeing work; a principal leads a school; a moment means a short time, not a fixed number of seconds.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 不计分虚构示例：“Some buses use electric power. Route 4 uses an electric bus. Route 9 uses an electric bus.” 主旨是有些巴士使用电力；4路和9路分别是支持例子。“没有巴士用电”与材料相反，例子也没有证明所有巴士都用电。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 不計分虛構示例：「Some buses use electric power. Route 4 uses an electric bus. Route 9 uses an electric bus.」主旨是有些巴士使用電力；4路和9路分別是支持例子。「沒有巴士用電」與材料相反，例子也沒有證明所有巴士都用電。
workedExample.en: Unscored made-up example: “Some buses use electric power. Route 4 uses an electric bus. Route 9 uses an electric bus.” Overall point: some buses use electric power. Route 4 is one supporting example; Route 9 is another. “No buses use electric power” contradicts the passage. The examples do not establish that all buses are electric.

Generally, we do not use “appeal” for normal, everyday requests. For example, we would not say:

I appeal for you to get some milk at the store.

But we would say something like:

The earthquake victims appealed to the government for more aid.

blocks.text:
Could you come here, please?

We might also be more exact about the meeting place. For example, a supervisor or principal might say:

Could you come to my office, please?

You might also be more exact with what you would like to do. For example, you might ask:

Could I talk to you for a moment?

These questions are very general, polite, and useful in a lot of situations.

teaching.zh-Hans: 主旨概括这段连贯材料在说明什么；细节或例子只支持其中一部分。用相关例子核对概括句，保留否定、can／may以及generally／probably等限制。细节即使真实，也可能不能回答主旨题。goal是目标，assignment是课程任务；originator是沟通发起者，audience是受众，anticipated是预期的，peers是同类群体中的人。录音中appeal是提出请求的动词，summon是叫人过来；aid是援助，victims是受不利事件影响的人，government是政府。supervisor是工作主管，principal是校长；a moment是短暂一会儿，不是固定秒数。
teaching.zh-Hant: 主旨概括這段連貫材料在說明什麼；細節或例子只支持其中一部分。用相關例子核對概括句，保留否定、can／may以及generally／probably等限制。細節即使真實，也可能不能回答主旨題。goal是目標，assignment是課程任務；originator是溝通發起者，audience是受眾，anticipated是預期的，peers是同類群體中的人。錄音中appeal是提出請求的動詞，summon是叫人過來；aid是援助，victims是受不利事件影響的人，government是政府。supervisor是工作主管，principal是校長；a moment是短暫一會兒，不是固定秒數。
teaching.en: A main point covers what the connected excerpt explains; a detail or example supports only part of it. Check a broad statement against all the relevant examples and keep negation, can/may and words such as generally or probably. A detail can be true and still fail a main-point question. Goal means an aim; an assignment is a course task. An originator starts communication; an audience receives it; anticipated means expected and peers are people in a similar group. In the recordings, appeal is a verb for making a request, while summon means call someone to come. Aid is help, victims are people affected by a harmful event, and government means the public authority. A supervisor is a person overseeing work; a principal leads a school; a moment means a short time, not a fixed number of seconds.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 不计分虚构示例：“Some buses use electric power. Route 4 uses an electric bus. Route 9 uses an electric bus.” 主旨是有些巴士使用电力；4路和9路分别是支持例子。“没有巴士用电”与材料相反，例子也没有证明所有巴士都用电。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 不計分虛構示例：「Some buses use electric power. Route 4 uses an electric bus. Route 9 uses an electric bus.」主旨是有些巴士使用電力；4路和9路分別是支持例子。「沒有巴士用電」與材料相反，例子也沒有證明所有巴士都用電。
workedExample.en: Unscored made-up example: “Some buses use electric power. Route 4 uses an electric bus. Route 9 uses an electric bus.” Overall point: some buses use electric power. Route 4 is one supporting example; Route 9 is another. “No buses use electric power” contradicts the passage. The examples do not establish that all buses are electric.

blocks.text: Most of the minerals that make up tehe rocks around us formed through the cooling of molten rock, known as magma. At the high temperatures that exist deep within Earth, some geological materials are liquid. As magma rises up through the crust, either by volcanic eruption or by more gradual processes, it cools and minerals crystallize. If the cooling process is rapid (minutes, hours, days, or years), the components of the minerals will not have time to become ordered and only small crystals can form before the rock becomes solid. The resulting rock will be fine-grained (i.e., with crystals less than 1 mm). If the cooling is slow (from decades to millions of years), the degree of ordering will be higher and relatively large crystals will form. In some cases, the cooling will be so fast (seconds) that the texture will be glassy, which means that no crystals at all form. Volcanic glass is not composed of minerals because the magma has cooled too rapidly for crystals to grow, although over time (millions of years) the volcanic glass may crystallize into various silicate minerals.

blocks.text: Researchers design studies to maximize reliability, which refers to how likely research results are to be replicated if the study is reproduced. Reliability increases the likelihood that what happens to one person will happen to all people in a group or what will happen in one situation will happen in another. Cooking is a science. When you follow a recipe and measure ingredients with a cooking tool, such as a measuring cup, the same results is obtained as long as the cook follows the same recipe and uses the same type of tool. The measuring cup introduces accuracy into the process. If a person uses a less accurate tool, such as their hand, to measure ingredients rather than a cup, the same result may not be replicated. Accurate tools and methods increase reliability.

teaching.en: Find what must be considered first (the condition), what follows under it (the outcome), and any stated reason. If does not establish that the condition has occurred. Keep may, not and only. A possible failure is neither inevitable failure nor guaranteed success. Compare the other stated condition and exceptions. Magma is molten rock; crystals have an ordered structure; solid means no longer liquid; fine-grained means small grains. Rapid means fast; a decade is ten years. Ingredients are the items used in a recipe; replicated means repeated with the same result; reliability here concerns repeatability. The source typo tehe means the.

workedExample.en: Unscored invented example: “If the parcel is too heavy, the drone may not take off because its motor cannot lift that load.” Condition: too heavy; possible outcome: no take-off; stated reason: motor capacity. Faithful answer: under that condition, take-off may fail. “It always fails” strengthens may; “it must take off” reverses the outcome; “if it is light” changes the condition. The sentence does not say this parcel is actually too heavy.

teaching.zh-Hans: 听条件、结果及说话者或叙述者给出的理由，保留if、not、because以及谁做什么、对谁产生感受。条件句不一定说明事情已经发生；过去叙事中的if也可表示“当……时／有时”。not because A but because B否认A是原因，改为B。背景：Anne向Matthew谈自己的包；另一叙述者描述Isabel与表兄Ralph。knack是窍门，worldly goods是财物，carpet-bag是老式旅行包；flagged是减弱／不那么高兴，ill-used是受到亏待，felt sorry for是同情，as a blind是作掩饰；little heart指缺乏热情，不是身体疾病。it seemed to her保留她的理解，没有证明他的动机。
teaching.zh-Hant: 聽條件、結果及說話者或敘述者給出的理由，保留if、not、because以及誰做什麼、對誰產生感受。條件句不一定說明事情已經發生；過去敘事中的if也可表示「當……時／有時」。not because A but because B否認A是原因，改為B。背景：Anne向Matthew談自己的包；另一敘述者描述Isabel與表兄Ralph。knack是竅門，worldly goods是財物，carpet-bag是老式旅行包；flagged是減弱／不那麼高興，ill-used是受到虧待，felt sorry for是同情，as a blind是作掩飾；little heart指缺乏熱情，不是身體疾病。it seemed to her保留她的理解，沒有證明他的動機。
teaching.en: Listen for the condition, its outcome and the reason stated by the speaker or narrator. Keep if, not, because and who does or feels what. A conditional statement need not describe something already done; in a narrated past account if can mean when or on occasions. Not because A but because B denies A as the reason and gives B instead. Background: Anne talks to Matthew about her bag; the other narrator describes Isabel and her cousin Ralph. Knack is a particular skill; worldly goods are possessions; a carpet-bag is an old travelling bag. Flagged means became less strong or cheerful, ill-used means mistreated, felt sorry for means pitied, and as a blind means as a cover; little heart means little enthusiasm, not a medical condition. It seemed to her preserves her interpretation, not his verified motive.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 不计分虚构示例：“If the parcel is too heavy, the drone may not take off because its motor cannot lift that load.” 条件是包裹过重，可能结果是无法起飞，所述原因是电机承载能力。忠实答案：在该条件下可能无法起飞。“总是失败”增强may，“一定起飞”颠倒结果，“包裹轻时”改变条件。句子没有说明这个包裹实际过重。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 不計分虛構示例：「If the parcel is too heavy, the drone may not take off because its motor cannot lift that load.」條件是包裹過重，可能結果是無法起飛，所述原因是電機承載能力。忠實答案：在該條件下可能無法起飛。「總是失敗」增強may，「一定起飛」顛倒結果，「包裹輕時」改變條件。句子沒有說明這個包裹實際過重。
workedExample.en: Unscored invented example: “If the parcel is too heavy, the drone may not take off because its motor cannot lift that load.” Condition: too heavy; possible outcome: no take-off; stated reason: motor capacity. Faithful answer: under that condition, take-off may fail. “It always fails” strengthens may; “it must take off” reverses the outcome; “if it is light” changes the condition. The sentence does not say this parcel is actually too heavy.

blocks.text: Surveys allow researchers to gather data from larger samples than may be afforded by other research methods. A sample is a subset of individuals selected from a population, which is the overall group of individuals that the researchers are interested in. Researchers study the sample and seek to generalize their findings to the population. Generally, researchers will begin this process by calculating various measures of central tendency from the data they have collected. These measures provide an overall summary of what a typical response looks like. There are three measures of central tendency: mode, median, and mean. The mode is the most frequently occurring response, the median lies at the middle of a given data set, and the mean is the arithmetic average of all data points. Means tend to be most useful in conducting additional analyses like those described below; however, means are very sensitive to the effects of outliers, and so one must be aware of those effects when making assessments of what measures of central tendency tell us about a data set in question.

blocks.text: The first step in archival research is typically to review a list or similar finding aid that indexes and describes the resources available in a collection. These descriptive aids can help researchers determine whether a collection contains resources that fit their needs and can make a visit to a selected archive more efficient and worthwhile. Finding aids have become so well constructed that they may provide researchers with enough information to enable the researcher to request copies of specific materials and avoid the effort and expense of traveling to the archive in person. Most archives offer downloadable finding aids of their most important collections on their websites, and there may be additional printed finding aids available on request. Most archives will make requested copies for a moderate fee and will mail or email researchers a packet of the reproduced materials. The cost of procuring such copies is almost always much less than the cost of traveling to an archive site and paying for housing and meals. However, if a collection is potentially full of material important to a research project, it may be better to visit in person.

blocks.text:
To Isabella, the relief of such tidings was very great, and they were scarcely less acceptable to Emma on her father’s account, who was immediately set as much at ease on the subject as his nervous constitution allowed; but the alarm that had been raised could not be appeased so as to admit of any comfort for him while he continued at Randalls. He was satisfied of there being no present danger in returning home, but no assurances could convince him that it was safe to stay; and while the others were variously urging and recommending, Mr. Knightley and Emma settled it in a few brief sentences: thus—

“Your father will not be easy; why do not you go?”

“I am ready, if the others are.”

“Shall I ring the bell?”

blocks.text:
Dorothy came to meet them and thanked the little mice warmly for saving her companion from death. She had grown so fond of the big Lion she was glad he had been rescued.

Then the mice were unharnessed from the truck and scampered away through the grass to their homes. The Queen of the Mice was the last to leave.

“If ever you need us again,” she said, “come out into the field and call, and we shall hear you and come to your assistance. Good-bye!”

“Good-bye!” they all answered, and away the Queen ran, while Dorothy held Toto tightly lest he should run after her and frighten her.

After this they sat down beside the Lion until he should awaken; and the Scarecrow brought Dorothy some fruit from a tree near by, which she ate for her dinner.

teaching.en: Identify the action or proposal, then connect its stated reason with exact context: a purpose, concern, preference or circumstance. Lest means to prevent a possible event; it does not say the event occurred. A proposal is not a completed action, and a reported belief is not independently verified fact. Keep each actor and time; another event nearby is not automatically the motive. Background: Toto is Dorothy’s dog; the Queen of the Mice is the mouse leader, and the Lion is another companion. Randalls is the house being visited in Emma. Unharnessed means released from pulling equipment; scampered means ran quickly; assistance is help; awaken means wake up. Tidings means news; constitution here concerns the father’s temperament; appeased means calmed; easy here means comfortable; assurances are words intended to reassure.

teaching.zh-Hans: 先找叙事中的动作或提议，再找明确相连的理由：目的、顾虑、偏好或当时情况。because和表示原因的as可以解释一个选择。保留he said、would rather ... than、not与决定的时点；附近细节不自动是动机，决定不等于已经完成行动。背景：一段是旅行者的叙述，另一段谈虚构河狸Brownie的房屋。ridge是狭长高地，lofty是高，patches是小片区域，advanced这里是进展，determined是决定，collect是采集；dwelling是住所，neat是整洁，dam是拦水的堤坝，与房屋不同；great-great-grandfather是高祖父。throw a dam across a stream这里是跨溪流修堤坝。
teaching.zh-Hant: 先找敘事中的動作或提議，再找明確相連的理由：目的、顧慮、偏好或當時情況。because和表示原因的as可以解釋一個選擇。保留he said、would rather ... than、not與決定的時點；附近細節不自動是動機，決定不等於已經完成行動。背景：一段是旅行者的敘述，另一段談虛構河狸Brownie的房屋。ridge是狹長高地，lofty是高，patches是小片區域，advanced這裡是進展，determined是決定，collect是採集；dwelling是住所，neat是整潔，dam是攔水的堤壩，與房屋不同；great-great-grandfather是高祖父。throw a dam across a stream這裡是跨溪流修堤壩。
teaching.en: Identify the narrated action or proposal and the reason explicitly connected to it: a purpose, concern, preference or circumstance. Because and a causal use of as can explain a choice. Preserve he said, would rather ... than, not and the time of the decision. A nearby detail is not automatically a motive, and a decision is not its completed action. Background: one excerpt is a traveller’s account; the other is about the house of Brownie, a fictional beaver. A ridge is narrow raised ground; lofty means high; patches are small areas; advanced here means progressed; determined means decided; collect means gather. A dwelling is a home; neat means tidy; a dam holds back water and is different from a house; great-great-grandfather means a grandfather’s grandfather. Throw a dam across a stream here means build it across the water.

workedExample.en: Unscored invented example: “Mina put the drawing in a folder so rain would not wet it. Afterward, she noticed a tear and decided to repair it.” Why use the folder? To keep the drawing dry. Repairing the tear is a later goal, not the stated purpose of the earlier action. Preventing rain damage does not prove it was raining or the drawing was wet. The text does not reveal every possible feeling Mina had.

blocks.text:
Anna: Hi there! And welcome to … Amelia, we don’t have a name for the show.

Amelia: We’ll think of a name later. For now, we'll call it “The Show.”

Anna: Great. Hi there! And welcome to “The Show.”

Anna: Today we are going to take you on a summer vacation! You will see popular things to do on vacation!

Anna: One is camping. When you go camping, you cook, sleep and play outdoors!

Amelia: When I go camping, Anna, I like to go hiking and fishing.

Anna: Me, too. Those are fun things to do when you go camping!

Anna: These people are hiking.

Amelia: Okay, let’s talk about the next vacation.

Anna: Another popular summer vacation is going to an amusement park. At an amusement park, you go on rides and eat lots of fun food!

Amelia: I love cotton candy … !

Anna & Amelia: and rollercoasters!

Amelia: This show is going to be a lot of fun.

blocks.text:
“And your father? Did you tell him?”

“Yes; and he seemed to think, with me, that something had happened, and that I should hear of Hosmer again. As he said, what interest could anyone have in bringing me to the doors of the church, and then leaving me? Now, if he had borrowed my money, or if he had married me and got my money settled on him, there might be some reason, but Hosmer was very independent about money and never would look at a shilling of mine. And yet, what could have happened? And why could he not write? Oh, it drives me half-mad to think of it, and I can’t sleep a wink at night.” She pulled a little handkerchief out of her muff and began to sob heavily into it.

“I shall glance into the case for you,” said Holmes, rising, “and I have no doubt that we shall reach some definite result. Let the weight of the matter rest upon me now, and do not let your mind dwell upon it further. Above all, try to let Mr. Hosmer Angel vanish from your memory, as he has done from your life.”

teaching.en: Read the whole exchange: who speaks to whom, what action is offered or announced, and which nearby words explain it. An undertaking can reassure; a programme introduction can present activities rather than physically take its audience somewhere. Figurative wording must fit its context. Future confidence is not a completed result, and a suggestion does not establish agreement or compliance. Background: Holmes is a detective speaking to a distressed visitor about the disappearance of Hosmer; Anna and Amelia are hosts in an educational skit. A case is an investigation; definite means clear; dwell upon means keep thinking about; a muff is a hand warmer; a shilling is an old money unit. Camping means staying outdoors; an amusement park has rides; cotton candy is a sweet; rollercoasters are rides.
teaching.zh-Hans: 读完整对话：谁对谁说话、提出或宣布什么行动、附近哪些话帮助理解。承担事务可以安抚别人，节目介绍可以展示活动，不一定真把观众带去某处；比喻需符合语境。对未来有信心不等于结果已完成，提议也不证明对方同意或照做。背景：Holmes是侦探，来访者因Hosmer失踪而困扰；Anna与Amelia是教学情境节目的主持人。case是调查的案件，definite是明确，dwell upon是反复想，muff是暖手筒，shilling是旧货币单位；camping是露营，amusement park是有游乐设施的公园，cotton candy是棉花糖，rollercoasters是过山车。
teaching.zh-Hant: 讀完整對話：誰對誰說話、提出或宣布什麼行動、附近哪些話幫助理解。承擔事務可以安撫別人，節目介紹可以展示活動，不一定真把觀眾帶去某處；比喻需符合語境。對未來有信心不等於結果已完成，提議也不證明對方同意或照做。背景：Holmes是偵探，來訪者因Hosmer失蹤而困擾；Anna與Amelia是教學情境節目的主持人。case是調查的案件，definite是明確，dwell upon是反覆想，muff是暖手筒，shilling是舊貨幣單位；camping是露營，amusement park是有遊樂設施的公園，cotton candy是棉花糖，rollercoasters是雲霄飛車。

workedExample.en: Unscored invented example: “The room list is missing,” said Lee. “Let me handle it. I’ll ask the librarian,” said Rina. What does Rina intend? She undertakes to ask the librarian, taking on the problem; she is not asking Lee to do it alone or reporting that the list is already found. teaching.zh-Hans: 听清谁对谁说话，以及话语在情境中做什么：承担行动、提出选项，还是报告事件。will可宣布未来安排，might可提出建议；结合附近问题、描述与背景，不把所有将来形式都当预测，也不把might只当不确定。保留行动者、时点与范围：意图不证明完成或同意。背景：一部历史小说中Prince of Conde对Edward说话，Worcester指较早的事件，不是当前说话者；另一部小说中West与寻找报社场地的人交谈。highly spoken of是受到称赞，retain是留下，services是所做的工作，by-and-by是以后；glanced是瞥看，negatively在这里描述摇头，mill是处理谷物的磨坊，turn it into是改作别的用途。录音中的完整句子属于更长的对话。
teaching.zh-Hant: 聽清誰對誰說話，以及話語在情境中做什麼：承擔行動、提出選項，還是報告事件。will可宣布未來安排，might可提出建議；結合附近問題、描述與背景，不把所有將來形式都當預測，也不把might只當不確定。保留行動者、時點與範圍：意圖不證明完成或同意。背景：一部歷史小說中Prince of Conde對Edward說話，Worcester指較早的事件，不是當前說話者；另一部小說中West與尋找報社場地的人交談。highly spoken of是受到稱讚，retain是留下，services是所做的工作，by-and-by是以後；glanced是瞥看，negatively在這裡描述搖頭，mill是處理穀物的磨坊，turn it into是改作別的用途。錄音中的完整句子屬於更長的對話。
teaching.en: Listen for who speaks to whom and what the words do in their situation: undertake an action, propose an option or report an event. Will can announce a future undertaking; might can offer a suggestion. Use nearby questions, descriptions and context rather than treating every future form as a prediction or every might as uncertainty alone. Keep actor, timing and scope: intention does not prove completion or agreement. Background: in one historical novel the Prince of Conde addresses Edward; Worcester names an earlier event, not the current speaker. In the other novel, West talks to people seeking newspaper premises. Highly spoken of means praised; retain means keep; services are work performed; by-and-by means later. Glanced means looked briefly; negatively here describes a head shake; a mill processes grain; turn it into means convert it to another use. The complete recorded sentences are parts of longer conversations.

blocks.text:
Players may move pieces out of their home onto their designated start space only when the die lands on 6. Getting a 6 at any point in the game also allows the player to take another turn, even if the player cannot move any of their pieces (as they cannot land on any of their own pieces). They also may move a new piece out even if they have another piece currently in play, and can also do the same if another player's piece is occupying their "start" space, but cannot do so when one of their own pieces is occupying their "start" space.

Pieces move clockwise around the track. Players can send opponents' pieces back to the start by landing on them. Teaming is not allowed in the game. Pieces are protected from capture after arriving in the final four slots of the finish area. Unlike more complex race games such as Parcheesi, counters cannot be maneuvered to block opponents' moves.

blocks.text: Letter tiles are arranged face-down into two piles; one all consonants, the other vowels. The contestant chooses a pile, and Vorderman reveals the top tile from that pile and places it on the board. A selection of nine tiles is generated in this way, and must contain at least three vowels and four consonants. Then, the clock is started and both contestants have thirty seconds to come up with the longest word they can make from the available letters. Each letter may be used only as often as it appears in the selection. The frequencies of the letters within each pile are weighted according to their frequency in natural English, in the same manner as Scrabble. For example, there are many Ns and Rs in the consonant pile, but only one Q.

teaching.en: Identify the intended task, what must be true before an action, what an exception blocks, and what remains allowed afterward. Then check every stage of the proposed plan against the instructions. Only when gives a necessary condition, not permission regardless of other rules; even if preserves a rule despite an obstacle. Then links stages. Keep numerical minima and reuse limits as well as order. Background: both texts describe recorded game rules. Home holds pieces not yet on the track; start is their entry space; a die is the numbered object rolled; clockwise follows a clock’s hands. A tile carries a letter; vowels and consonants are the two named letter groups; face-down hides the letter. A presenter named in an old snapshot is not a current-role claim.

teaching.zh-Hans: 跟随完整录音阶段：确定起始材料、相连行动、退出条件与有无时间重叠。until给出停止重复的条件，不是固定重复次数；while允许活动重叠，不要求起止时点相同。核对完整计划的每部分，包括对象、顺序与约量。材料是历史食谱描述：一段以已准备的鱼肉和酱汁开始，另一段以正在煮的禽肉开始；更早准备与后续完成未录入。baking-dish是入炉容器，layer是层，grated nutmeg是磨碎的肉豆蔻调料，crumbs是面包屑，dot with butter是放小块黄油，brown是在炉内使表面上色；fowl是作食材的禽类，spice bag是香料袋，pickles是腌菜。Crisco是原文历史油脂选项名称，不是推荐。
teaching.zh-Hant: 跟隨完整錄音階段：確定起始材料、相連行動、退出條件與有無時間重疊。until給出停止重複的條件，不是固定重複次數；while允許活動重疊，不要求起止時點相同。核對完整計畫的每部分，包括對象、順序與約量。材料是歷史食譜描述：一段以已準備的魚肉和醬汁開始，另一段以正在煮的禽肉開始；更早準備與後續完成未錄入。baking-dish是入爐容器，layer是層，grated nutmeg是磨碎的肉豆蔻調料，crumbs是麵包屑，dot with butter是放小塊奶油，brown是在爐內使表面上色；fowl是作食材的禽類，spice bag是香料袋，pickles是醃菜。Crisco是原文歷史油脂選項名稱，不是推薦。
teaching.en: Follow the whole recorded stage: identify its starting materials, linked actions, exit condition and any overlap. Until gives the condition for stopping a repeated action, not a fixed repetition count. While permits overlapping activity, not necessarily equal start/end times. Check every part of a proposed plan, including objects, order and approximate amounts. These are historical recipe descriptions: one stage begins with prepared fish and sauce; another begins with fowl already cooking. Earlier preparation and later completion are not recorded. A baking-dish is an oven container; a layer is one covering level; grated nutmeg is a ground seasoning; crumbs are small pieces of bread; dot with butter means add small pieces; brown means give the surface colour in the oven. A fowl is a bird used for food; a spice bag holds seasonings; pickles are preserved vegetables. Crisco is a historical named fat alternative in the source, not a recommendation.

materials.title: Conquering the World: The Invasion of the Red Swamp Crayfish

blocks.text: We live in a changing world, where we can travel over great distances more easily and quickly than ever before. Humans have accidentally, or intentionally, transported lots of species out of their natural homes, or native ranges, for centuries. However, the frequency of such events has drastically increased in recent decades. Many species end up being released into new environments where they can survive, reproduce successfully, and become invasive, which means they begin to outcompete native species [1]. Invasive alien species can cause severe problems for the environment, the economy, and human well-being. For example, the accumulation of zebra mussel (Dreissena polymorpha) shells in water intake pipes used for irrigation of fields can block the pipes and cause the farmers to lose large amounts of money. As another example, the digging activity of a fish called the common carp (Cyprinus carpio) increases the cloudiness of the water, which can reduce the ability of aquatic plants to perform photosynthesis by decreasing the amount of light that reaches them. Given their serious impacts, invasive alien species are considered one of the greatest threats to biodiversity, ecosystem services and human well-being.

materials.title: How do Scientists Use Sound to Count Fish in The Deep Sea?

blocks.text: Interpreting echograms takes a lot of experience and sometimes scientists make mistakes. For example, echograms were used to make ocean maps to help prevent ships from running aground on the seafloor. Sometimes an echogram would show that a part of the sea was shallow enough to be dangerous for boats. These shallow areas were marked on a map so that other boats could avoid them. However, another captain returning to the same area would find that the water was much deeper than the map showed. Scientists later learned that some areas that were mapped as having shallow sea floors actually contained dense layers of sea life, made up of fish and jellyfish [2]. There was so much marine life in the water that the echo from all the animals together sounded the same as the echo from the sea floor! While scientists knew that they could use sound to locate fish in the water [3], they did not expect to find so many animals so close together. Luckily, mistakes in science can lead to new discoveries. In this case, scientists learned that what they thought was the sea floor was actually dense clusters of marine animals!

blocks.text: The proclamation generated quick and dramatic reactions. The news created euphoria among enslaved people, as it signaled the eventual end of their bondage. Predictably, Confederate leaders raged against the proclamation, reinforcing their commitment to fight to maintain slavery, the foundation of the Confederacy. In the North, opinions split widely on the issue. Abolitionists praised Lincoln’s actions, which they saw as the fulfillment of their long campaign to strike down an immoral institution. But other Northerners, especially Irish, working-class, urban dwellers loyal to the Democratic Party and others with racist beliefs, hated the new goal of emancipation and found the idea of freed formerly enslaved people repugnant. At its core, much of this racism had an economic foundation: Many Northerners feared competing with emancipated people for scarce jobs.

credit.attribution: U.S. History — P. Scott Corbett; Jay Precht; Volker Janssen; John M. Lund; Todd Pfannestiel; Paul Vickery; Sylvie Waskiewicz. OpenStax, Rice University. CC BY 4.0; fixed source edition; whitespace normalised, separate paragraphs. — 1863: The Changing Nature of the War
credit.license: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); original prose only, excluding third-party material and media.

blocks.text: Given the remarkable complexity of a language, one might expect that mastering a language would be an especially arduous task; indeed, for those of us trying to learn a second language as adults, this might seem to be true. However, young children master language very quickly with relative ease. B. F. Skinner (1957) proposed that language is learned through reinforcement. Noam Chomsky (1965) criticized this behaviorist approach, asserting instead that the mechanisms underlying language acquisition are biologically determined. The use of language develops in the absence of formal instruction and appears to follow a very similar pattern in children from vastly different cultures and backgrounds. It would seem, therefore, that we are born with a biological predisposition to acquire a language (Chomsky, 1965; Fernández & Cairns, 2011). Moreover, it appears that there is a critical period for language acquisition, such that this proficiency at acquiring language is maximal early in life; generally, as people age, the ease with which they acquire and master new languages diminishes (Johnson & Newport, 1989; Lenneberg, 1967; Singleton, 1995).

blocks.text:
Historians studying the ancient period examine the emergence of the first major civilizations in regions such as Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Indus Valley, China, and Peru, beginning approximately 3500 BCE in some regions. The new social, economic, and political complexities necessitated the development of writing systems. Thanks to advancements in agriculture, surplus food allowed these civilizations to support larger populations, leading to urbanization, the establishment of trade networks, and the emergence of regional empires. In the later part of the ancient period, sometimes termed the classical period, societies in China, India, Persia, and the Mediterranean expanded further, reaching new cultural, scientific, and political heights. Meanwhile, influential religious systems and philosophical ideas were first formulated, such as Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Judaism, and Greek philosophy.

In the study of post-classical or medieval history, which began around 500 CE, historians note the growing influence of major religions. Missionary religions, like Buddhism, Christianity, and Islam, spread rapidly and established themselves as world religions, marking a cultural shift as they gradually replaced other belief systems. Meanwhile, inter-regional trade networks flourished, leading to increased technological and cultural exchange. Conquering many territories in Asia and Europe, the Mongol Empire became a dominant force during the 13th and 14th centuries.

Historians focused on early modern history, which started roughly in 1500 CE, commonly highlight how European states rose to global power. As gunpowder empires, they explored and colonized large parts of the world. As a result, the Americas were integrated into the global network, triggering a vast biological exchange of plants, animals, people, and diseases. The Scientific Revolution prompted major discoveries and accelerated technological progress. It was accompanied by other intellectual developments, such as humanism and the Enlightenment, which ushered in secularization.

In the study of modern history, which began at the end of the 18th century, historians are interested in how the Industrial Revolution transformed economies by introducing more efficient modes of production. Western powers established vast colonial empires, gaining superiority through industrialized military technology. The increased international exchange of goods, ideas, and people marked the beginning of globalization. Various social revolutions challenged autocratic and colonial regimes, paving the way for democracies. Many developments in fields like science, technology, economy, living standards, and human population accelerated at unprecedented rates. This happened despite the widespread destruction caused by two world wars, which rebalanced international power relations by undermining European dominance.

blocks.text:
Web content providers also manipulated a number of attributes within the HTML source of a page in an attempt to rank well in search engines.

By relying so much on factors exclusively within a webmaster's control, early search engines suffered from abuse and ranking manipulation. To provide better results to their users, search engines had to adapt to ensure their results pages showed the most relevant search results, rather than unrelated pages stuffed with numerous keywords by unscrupulous webmasters. Since the success and popularity of a search engine is determined by its ability to produce the most relevant results to any given search allowing those results to be false would turn users to find other search sources. Search engines responded by developing more complex ranking algorithms, taking into account additional factors that were more difficult for webmasters to manipulate.

Graduate students at Stanford University, Larry Page and Sergey Brin developed "backrub", a search engine that relied on a mathematical algorithm to rate the prominence of web pages. The number calculated by the algorithm, PageRank, is a function of the quantity and strength of inbound links. PageRank estimates the likelihood that a given page will be reached by a web user who randomly surfs the web, and follows links from one page to another. In effect, this means that some links are stronger than others, as a higher PageRank page is more likely to be reached by the random surfer.

Page and Brin founded Google in 1998. Google attracted a loyal following among the growing number of Internet users, who liked its simple design. Off-page factors such as PageRank and hyperlink analysis were considered, as well as on-page factors, to enable Google to avoid the kind of manipulation seen in search engines that only considered on-page factors for their rankings.

teaching.zh-Hans: 先找较概括的主张，再看具体例子在所在位置做什么：说明某类影响、展示可能的错误，或解释一项发现。保留对象、类别、时期，以及can、some、gradually等限制。例子说明特定一点，不单凭自己证明所有情况或无限制的因果。同一个词或事件可能出现在不同主张之下，须看此处承接句，不能只配关键词。本题匹配例子在该处被直接赋予的作用，而非它也可能关联的每个观点。 背景：History按该文分类概述古代、中世纪、近代早期与现代，BCE／CE标记历法年份；formulation是形成，spread是传播到更多地方。humanism与Enlightenment是思想发展名称。另一份历史叙述中，HTML是网页代码，webmaster管理网站，ranking把搜索结果排序；on-page在页面内，off-page包括其他页面传入的链接。PageRank是文中所述历史随机浏览模型，不是当前SEO建议。须跨段重听，区分被列举的对象与其说明的概括主张。
teaching.zh-Hant: 先找較概括的主張，再看具體例子在所在位置做什麼：說明某類影響、展示可能的錯誤，或解釋一項發現。保留對象、類別、時期，以及can、some、gradually等限制。例子說明特定一點，不單憑自己證明所有情況或無限制的因果。同一個詞或事件可能出現在不同主張之下，須看此處承接句，不能只配關鍵詞。本題匹配例子在該處被直接賦予的作用，而非它也可能關聯的每個觀點。 背景：History按該文分類概述古代、中世紀、近代早期與現代，BCE／CE標記曆法年份；formulation是形成，spread是傳播到更多地方。humanism與Enlightenment是思想發展名稱。另一份歷史敘述中，HTML是網頁程式碼，webmaster管理網站，ranking把搜尋結果排序；on-page在頁面內，off-page包括其他頁面傳入的連結。PageRank是文中所述歷史隨機瀏覽模型，不是當前SEO建議。須跨段重聽，區分被列舉的對象與其說明的概括主張。
teaching.en: Find the broader claim, then ask what the particular example does at that point: illustrate a kind of effect, show a possible mistake, or explain a discovery. Keep its actor, category, period and words such as can, some and gradually. An example supports a particular point; it does not by itself prove every case or an unlimited cause. The same word or episode can appear under different claims, so use the local framing statement rather than matching keywords alone. In this task, match the example’s directly framed role, not every idea it could also relate to. Background: History surveys the ancient, medieval, early-modern and modern periods using the passage’s categories; BCE/CE label calendar years. Formulation means first development, while spread means reaching more places. Humanism and the Enlightenment name intellectual developments. In the other historical account, HTML is web-page code, a webmaster manages a website, and ranking orders search results. On-page factors are within a page; off-page factors include links from other pages. PageRank is the historical random-surfer model described, not current SEO advice. Listen across paragraphs to distinguish a named example from the broader claim it illustrates.

workedExample.zh-Hans: 不计分虚构示例：“Sellers use different ways to reach customers. One uses a website; another attends a local fair. These options can still fail. Mina attended a fair but made no sales.” 网站与第一次提到的集市说明不同接触顾客的方法；Mina在集市没有卖出东西，承接前句，说明方法可能失败。fair重复出现，不表示两处作用相同；一次失败也不证明每次集市都失败。
workedExample.zh-Hant: 不計分虛構示例：「Sellers use different ways to reach customers. One uses a website; another attends a local fair. These options can still fail. Mina attended a fair but made no sales.」網站與第一次提到的市集說明不同接觸顧客的方法；Mina在市集沒有賣出東西，承接前句，說明方法可能失敗。fair重複出現，不表示兩處作用相同；一次失敗也不證明每次市集都失敗。
workedExample.en: Unscored invented example: “Sellers use different ways to reach customers. One uses a website; another attends a local fair. These options can still fail. Mina attended a fair but made no sales.” The website and the first fair illustrate different outreach methods. Mina’s unsuccessful fair illustrates possible failure, as framed by the preceding sentence. The repeated word fair does not give both examples the same role; one failure does not prove every fair fails.

explanation.zh-Hans: 第一组列举说明古代部分所述的思想与信仰体系形成，第二组说明中世纪部分传教宗教的传播。Buddhism在两组都出现，不能只凭这个词决定作用：“形成”与后来的“传播”是不同主张。humanism与Enlightenment说明近代早期伴随科学革命的思想发展。这是原文的时期分类，不表示所有地区日期相同，或早先信仰全部消失。

explanation.en: The first list illustrates systems described as first formulated in the ancient-period account; the second illustrates missionary religions spreading in the medieval account. Buddhism occurs in both, so the word alone cannot determine the role: formulation and later spread are different claims. Humanism and the Enlightenment illustrate intellectual developments accompanying the Scientific Revolution in the early-modern account. These are the passage’s period categories, not identical dates for every region or proof all earlier beliefs vanished.

materials.title: How Many Ways Are There to Make a Black Hole?

credit.attribution: How Many Ways Are There to Make a Black Hole? — Shamit Kachru. Frontiers for Young Minds. CC BY 4.0; complete original native paragraphs, whitespace normalised; media and third-party quotations excluded.
credit.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Article-specific original grant; images, quoted third-party text and excluded material omitted.

blocks.text: The entropy in a physical system is a measure of the amount of messiness or arbitrariness characterizing the system. Systems in very special states—almost any hunk of normal matter at very low temperatures, or a very clean bedroom, for instance—have low entropy. In both cases this is because the constituents of the system have no choice about where to be. At low temperature, in a chunk of material, every atom sits at a place that minimizes the energy of the system. In a very clean room, every piece of clothing is folded and stacked in a drawer. In contrast, matter at high temperature, or a messy room, has high entropy. The atoms can be flying about every which way in hot matter. In a messy bedroom, shirts and shorts can be flung about the room willy nilly. The entropy of a system is defined as the logarithm of the number of possible configurations of its constituents (atoms for matter; shirts and shorts for the messy room) that would look roughly the same, to a casual observer.

credit.attribution: Explore More! How New Environments May Boost Your Memory — Kreeta I. L. Kerkkänen; Marit F. L. Ruitenberg; Judith Schomaker. Frontiers for Young Minds. CC BY 4.0; complete original native paragraphs, whitespace normalised; media and third-party quotations excluded.

blocks.text: Previous studies suggest that being immersed in or witnessing anything novel activates brain areas important in the production of dopamine. Dopamine is one of the chemical messengers that neurons use to talk to one another. The main task of dopamine is to anticipate the value of things in our environment. For example, dopamine helps us to evaluate how rewarding certain objects, people, or experiences are, and helps us better remember the things that are important or rewarding. You could picture dopamine as a ranger deciding which paths in the forest (memories) are especially important and then making these paths more walkable (easier to remember). The brain areas responsible for producing dopamine mature throughout childhood and adolescence, leading to more dopamine rangers working in our brain during that time in our lives. In contrast, as we become older, these areas begin to retire and—just like humans do—lose some of their productivity, resulting in less dopamine in the brain [2].

exactEvidence: Previous studies suggest that being immersed in or witnessing anything novel activates brain areas important in the production of dopamine. Dopamine is one of the chemical messengers that neurons use to talk to one another. The main task of dopamine is to anticipate the value of things in our environment. For example, dopamine helps us to evaluate how rewarding certain objects, people, or experiences are, and helps us better remember the things that are important or rewarding. You could picture dopamine as a ranger deciding which paths in the forest (memories) are especially important and then making these paths more walkable (easier to remember). The brain areas responsible for producing dopamine mature throughout childhood and adolescence, leading to more dopamine rangers working in our brain during that time in our lives. In contrast, as we become older, these areas begin to retire and—just like humans do—lose some of their productivity, resulting in less dopamine in the brain [2].

exactEvidence: The entropy in a physical system is a measure of the amount of messiness or arbitrariness characterizing the system. Systems in very special states—almost any hunk of normal matter at very low temperatures, or a very clean bedroom, for instance—have low entropy. In both cases this is because the constituents of the system have no choice about where to be. At low temperature, in a chunk of material, every atom sits at a place that minimizes the energy of the system. In a very clean room, every piece of clothing is folded and stacked in a drawer. In contrast, matter at high temperature, or a messy room, has high entropy. The atoms can be flying about every which way in hot matter. In a messy bedroom, shirts and shorts can be flung about the room willy nilly. The entropy of a system is defined as the logarithm of the number of possible configurations of its constituents (atoms for matter; shirts and shorts for the messy room) that would look roughly the same, to a casual observer.
